Trees and power lines blown down by winds estimated at 70 MPH.

Numerous trees, large tree limbs, and power poles were downed. A tree fell on a carport on FM 36 near Caddo Mills. Another roof collapsed near the vicinity of Polk and Pickett Streets in Greenville. In Celeste, a tree fell on the covered parking at a church.
Roof damage and power outages were reported.
Large tree limbs and power lines were blown down on Park Street in Commerce. Trees were also blown down on Highway 24 northeast of town.
The ground was covered with penny-size hail.
Quarter-size hail was reported in Greenville.
A large tree was uprooted and fell onto a house and a peach tree. The house suffered roof and wall damage. Another tree fell in the town center of Greenville.

A tornado was observed on the ground by a broadcast meteorologist for 3-4 minutes before becoming rain wrapped. No damage was reported.

Trees were knocked down on Rancho Road.

A microburst damaged part of the southern portions of the city of Greenville. Several businesses and residential structures sustained roof damage. The roof of a Braum's was heavily damaged, and the roof at an automobile service station on Business 67 was partially blown off. In a…

Thunderstorm winds produced widespread damage near Quinlan and across areas south of Greenville in Hunt County. The strongest hit areas were along a line from near Cash to Lone Oak. Winds downed numerous trees, power lines and damaged several structures in these areas.

A brief tornado was observed south of Interstate 30 between Campbell and Cumby. This tornado occurred in open country and was rated at EF-0.

A strong EF-2 tornado began in eastern Rockwall County and traveled northeast into Hunt County before lifting. As the tornado crossed into Hunt County, it destroyed one mobile home near the Rockwall/Hunt County Line. The tornado then continued to the northeast where it destroyed …

Several trained storm spotters observed and reported a tornado over open country approximately 6 miles south of Greenville. This EF-0 tornado had maximum estimated winds of approximately 80 mph, a path length of approximately half a mile, and a path width of 50 yards.

Damaging thunderstorm winds damaged the roof and structure of a barn located approximately 2 miles south of Greenville. A large section of property fence was also knocked down, an RV was overturned, and large trees were uprooted on the same property.
Golf ball sized hail was reported at Interstate 30 and Highway 34; south of Greenville.
